title: KV Slab Collapser and Compact Hotpath Rewriter
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Introduce a compacting pass and hotpath rewrite in the KV slab allocator to collapse duplicate prompt fragments across concurrent requests, reduce GPU-resident KV footprint, and improve continuous-batching throughput without increasing tail latency.
background: Observed multi-tenant workloads with interleaved small prompts cause slab fragmentation and duplicate KV fragments across slots. This increases GPU memory usage and reduces effective batch size. Existing heuristics dedupe only at coarse granularity; we need a runtime aware collapser that operates in the hot path and can be applied opportunistically during batch formation.
goals: 1) Reduce GPU KV memory for multi-tenant LRU slabs by at least 22-30% in 95% of observed traffic patterns. 2) Maintain 99p latency within current SLO (+2ms tolerance). 3) Avoid impacting correctness of KV reads/writes across pinned sessions and model variants.
non_goals: Do not change on-disk checkpoint formats or cross-node snapshot semantics. This ticket does not implement cross-region cache sharing.
design_decisions: We will implement a two-stage approach: a fast in-memory fingerprint compactor executed during batch assembly that does lightweight equality checks (64-bit rolling hash) and an optional background slab-collapser job that reclaims duplicate fragments at larger granularity. Deduplication will be content-addressable and reference-counted to maintain per-session isolation. To avoid expensive synchronization, the hotpath will use epoch-based ownership tokens and atomic refcount ops.
tradeoffs:
- Aggressive dedupe can increase CPU work when assembling batches; we limit checks to top-N frequent fragment candidates per slot.
- Using 64-bit fingerprints risks collisions; mitigated by a second-stage short canonical verification for candidates above threshold.
- Reference counting introduces extra writes to GPU memory; we amortize via slab-level counter batching.
acceptance_criteria: Memory reduction: 22-30% median decrease in GPU KV bytes for sampled multi-tenant trace (runbook dataset)
Latency: no more than +2ms median increase and +5ms for P99 compared to baseline on continuous-batching benchmark (1k requests/sec mixed sequences)
Correctness: full KV read/write regression suite passes; no cross-session leakage observed in chaos tests
Operational: metrics exported for dedupe-hit-rate, compactor-cpu-ms, refcount-ops/sec, and reclaimed-bytes; alert thresholds defined
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype lightweight 64-bit rolling fingerprint generation for tokenized prompt fragments (engine module)
2) Implement hotpath comparator at batch assemble that identifies top-3 candidate matches per request slot and swaps in shared reference when safe
3) Add atomic slab refcount field and batched decrement/compact path
4) Build background slab-collapser that merges low-churn duplicates during low-util windows
5) Integrate metrics/tracing and add canary rollout flags behind runtime config
6) End-to-end tests and perf runs against replay traces; iterate on thresholds
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and canonical verification
Integration tests: multi-tenant KV isolation, concurrent refcount updates
Performance: run continuous-batching perf harness with and without collapser on GPU instance types G4/G5-equivalent; capture P50/P95/P99 and memory usage
Chaos: simulate mid-batch eviction and node OOM to validate refcount cleanup and background compactor recovery
Compatibility: regression across model variants (gpt-small/gpt-medium) to verify canonicalization rules
rollback_strategy: Feature guarded by runtime flag. If production canary shows >5% increase in tail latency or memory regression, flip flag off and trigger immediate background compactor run to rebuild expected state. Deploy rollback playbook that clears transient refcounts and restores previous slab layout via checkpoint load if needed.
rollout_plan: Dev: local + CI with synthetic traces
Staging: 10% traffic on non-critical tenants for 48h with detailed metrics
Canary: 1% traffic on mixed workloads for 24h; validate acceptance criteria
Ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 24h holds and automated alerts

notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative on CPU work in the hotpath. If we need more aggressive dedupe later, we can expose tunable N for candidate selection and enable per-tenant aggressive mode behind tenant config. Long-term follow-up: evaluate content-aware compression for merged fragments.
